question.prompt:
Point \(E\) is selected on side \(AB\) of triangle \(ABC\) in such a way that \(AE:EB=1:3,\) and point \(D\) is selected on side \(BC\) so that \(CD:DB=1:2.\) The point of intersection of \(AD\) and \(CE\) is \(F.\) Then

\[ \frac{EF}{FC}+\frac{AF}{FD} \]

is:

[Figure 1](figures/1965_AMC_12_Q37_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
A line through \(D\) parallel to \(CE\) transfers the ratio on \(BC\) to \(AB\), where we already know another ratio. Draw this line, meeting \(AB\) at \(H\).

Triangles \(BDH\) and \(BCE\) are similar by AA: they share the angle at \(B\), and \(DH\parallel CE\). Therefore
\[
\frac{BH}{BE}=\frac{DH}{CE}=\frac{BD}{BC}=\frac23.
\]
Let \(AE=e>0\). Then \(EB=3e\), \(AB=4e\), and the displayed proportion gives \(BH=2e\). Hence \(AH=4e-2e=2e\), making \(E\) the midpoint of \(AH\).

Now \(EF\parallel HD\), so triangles \(AEF\) and \(AHD\) are similar by AA. Their scale factor is \(AE/AH=1/2\), giving
\[
\frac{AF}{AD}=\frac{EF}{HD}=\frac12.
\]
Thus \(AF=FD\). Also, \(HD=\frac23 CE\), so
\[
EF=\frac12 HD=\frac13 CE,
\qquad FC=\frac23 CE.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{EF}{FC}+\frac{AF}{FD}
=\frac12+1=\boxed{\frac32},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Transfer the ratio with a parallel line

solutions.explanation:
Triangles with the same altitude have areas in the ratio of their bases. This lets us use both given side ratios without constructing another line. Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of triangle \(XYZ\), and set
\[
[AEF]=x,\qquad [ACF]=y.
\]
Both \(x\) and \(y\) are positive because the two cevians meet inside the triangle.

Triangles \(AEF\) and \(BEF\) have the same altitude to \(AB\), so \([BEF]=3x\). Likewise, \([BEC]=3[AEC]\), since their bases \(BE\) and \(AE\) have ratio \(3:1\) and they share the altitude from \(C\). As \([AEC]=x+y\), subtraction gives
\[
[BFC]=3(x+y)-3x=3y.
\]
Triangles \(BFD\) and \(CFD\) share the altitude from \(F\) to \(BC\), so their areas have ratio \(BD:CD=2:1\). Together they make triangle \(BFC\), whose area is \(3y\). Therefore
\[
[CFD]=y,\qquad [BFD]=2y.
\]
Finally, triangles \(ABD\) and \(ACD\) share the altitude from \(A\) to \(BC\), so \([ABD]=2[ACD]\). Splitting these triangles at \(F\) gives
\[
4x+2y=2(y+y),
\]
so \(y=2x\).

Using common altitudes once more, now with bases on \(CE\) and \(AD\), respectively, we obtain
\[
\frac{EF}{FC}=\frac{[AEF]}{[ACF]}=\frac{x}{y}=\frac12,
\]
\[
\frac{AF}{FD}=\frac{[ACF]}{[CDF]}=\frac{y}{y}=1.
\]
Thus the requested sum is \(\boxed{\frac32}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Compare triangle areas
